children: Bernstein maintains its positive assessment of Usnoflast’s probability of success

Shares of Zydus Lifesciences gained nearly 2 per cent in Friday’s trade after Bernstein said Novartis’ decision to discontinue development of its experimental amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) drug had improved the commercial opportunity for Zydus’ Usnoflast.

Zydus Life shares rose as much as 2.8 per cent to Rs 1,167.30 on the NSE before paring some gains. The stock was trading at Rs 1,155.80, up 1.82 per cent, at 11:17 am. It opened at Rs 1,150.70 and touched an intraday low of Rs 1,147.70.

Bernstein retained its Outperform rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 1,457. The brokerage’s assessment follows Novartis’ September 16 decision to discontinue VHB937, also known as lifonebart, after the drug failed to meet the primary and secondary endpoints in a Phase II trial for ALS. The study involved 251 patients with early-stage ALS.

According to Bernstein, the withdrawal of VHB937 could give Usnoflast a clearer commercial opportunity in the ALS market. However, the brokerage said the key determinant of the drug’s value remains its ability to demonstrate a clinically meaningful slowing of disease progression in the ongoing UNITE-ALS study.
The two drugs work through different biological pathways, Bernstein noted, and the brokerage maintained its positive assessment of Usnoflast’s probability of success.

Usnoflast is Zydus Life’s novel chemical entity candidate being developed for ALS. The company has previously received US Food and Drug Administration approval to conduct Phase II(b) trials for the drug, while Usnoflast has also received Orphan Drug Designation for ALS in the US.

Bernstein expects Usnoflast to demonstrate meaningful efficacy in its Phase II(b) trial. It estimates that the drug could eventually generate an annual revenue run rate of around USD 100 million, supported by its oral formulation and potential applicability across a broad ALS patient population.
Bernstein also expects Usnoflast to ramp up faster than Zydus’ Saroglitazar and potentially become the company’s second high-return US new chemical entity.
The brokerage said Zydus was steadily expanding its innovation pipeline to support growth in the US market.

Zydus has been developing Usnoflast across multiple indications. The company describes the molecule as an oral NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitor and has been evaluating it for ALS, Parkinson’s disease, ulcerative colitis and cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes.
